question: Do price jumps in decentralized prediction markets causally amplify media attention and induce self-fulfilling electoral expectations?
scope: 2024 US Presidential Election across 7 key battleground states (PA, MI, WI, AZ, GA, NV, NC) combining daily Polymarket CLOB settlement prices, 538 state polling averages, and public attention indices

searches.query: prediction market media coverage reflexivity election odds
rational inattention media gatekeeping price jumps bandwagon
identification through heteroskedasticity simultaneous equations Rigobon
Polymarket central limit order book election microstructure swing states

nearest_works.title: Prediction Markets
nearest_works.question: How accurately do prediction markets aggregate private information compared to traditional polling?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Information aggregation efficiency and forecast unbiasedness
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Descriptive time-series and correlation analysis of Iowa Electronic Markets
nearest_works.difference: Examines prediction markets as passive information aggregators; does not model or identify bi-directional media feedback or reflexivity.

nearest_works.title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?
nearest_works.question: Does prediction market price discovery stem from widespread crowd wisdom or concentrated informed capital?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Price response to large trades and market participant informativeness
nearest_works.method_or_proof: High-frequency Kyle lambda and order-flow Kyle decomposition
nearest_works.difference: Focuses strictly on internal market trading microstructure without examining downstream media reporting amplification or voter expectation feedback.

nearest_works.title: The Anatomy of Polymarket: Trading, Media, and Voter Sentiment
nearest_works.question: How do Polymarket betting odds correlate with news sentiment and voter preferences during presidential elections?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Co-movement and reduced-form lead-lag correlations between betting odds, news volume, and polls
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Standard OLS panel regressions and Whale trader instrumental variables
nearest_works.difference: Relies on invalid whale-trade IVs that violate exclusion restrictions due to global media visibility; does not address simultaneous dynamic feedback bias or solve bi-directional causality via structural heteroskedasticity (Rigobon).

contribution_statement: First study to formally establish theoretical micro-foundations of market-media reflexivity (Kyle-Sims-Callander dynamic Bayesian game) and to solve simultaneous bi-directional causality between prediction market odds and media attention using Rigobon (2003) structural heteroskedasticity identification on a 7-battleground-state daily panel.
limitations: Empirical sample is confined to the 2024 US Presidential Election across 7 swing states.
Direct voter ballot choices cannot be tracked at high frequency, requiring polling margins and public platform attention as empirical proxies.
Structural identification assumes constancy of structural transmission parameters across high- and low-volatility event regimes.
